B70 bring-up and thermal checks — 2026-10-23

This iteration prioritised working inference. No throughput benchmark, full-window quality test or sustained thermal-stability test was performed. All results below are bounded functional checks on the newly installed card.

Live B70 result

  • Bigcachy detects Intel Arc Pro B70 at PCI 0000:04:00.0, ID 8086:e223, xe driver.
  • The OS maps a full 32 GiB memory BAR. Explicit PCI capability decoding requires sudo; the full aperture provides evidence that the intended large BAR is active.
  • Driver-reported usable GPU memory: 31.890625 GiB. Earlier prepared estimates assumed 32; the staged Muse 1696k/two-slot ceiling must be recalculated before use.
  • Native Vulkan llama.cpp v0.7.0, exact pinned commit 620d2225cc436ab0b001e3200e590e3b286ef9ab, is bound only to vendor 8086/device e223 and discrete type. Missing/ambiguous devices fail closed; no iGPU/RTX fallback.
  • Pinned Qwen Q4 weights were copied from the existing Geekom XFS store and verified against their SHA256. No replacement of the Geekom backend occurred.
  • First authenticated b70 - 256k 2 slots - qwen3.8 smrt · KV4 request returned OK. Native child slots each reported 262144 tokens; OpenCode limit is 258048.
  • Actual OpenCode inference returned B70 OK, with no tool use or file edits.
  • The profile is selectable on Bigcachy, l-dev-ai and mini-mobile. Each client has a separate registered inference-only key, checked against the live gateway.
  • The other twelve B70 profiles are disabled in owner policy and excluded by the client allowlist until checked. They are not certified by the first profile test.

Separate devices and reboot behavior

Arc has its own arcB70.service backend, lario-admission@arcB70.service gateway, loopback backend port 11447, public authenticated port 11437 and independent control state. Both units are enabled; the XFS mount, physical device and durable Off intent are checked before starting. The proxy starts cold and loads the saved fixed profile on its first valid request. Actual cold-boot validation remains pending. The RTX backend was not restarted or used for the Arc test. Existing Intel CPU embedding, NPU Whisper, iGPU translation and CPU TTS health checks remained healthy.

One-minute passive thermal observation

The B70 is installed above the RTX with a gap between cards. Both were monitored while only Arc inference was exercised; no artificial simultaneous GPU workload, fan override or power-limit change was applied.

Observation B70 package B70 VRAM RTX GPU
Initial idle 37 C 42 C 30 C
First short model load/request 43 C 46 C 30 C
Peak over 30 samples / 60 seconds during OpenCode check 59 C 64 C 31 C

The initial B70 fan was 1404 RPM, rising to 1536 RPM after first load; RTX was idle at about 24 W with its fans stopped. These temperatures show no immediate problem in this short check. They cannot establish sustained case airflow, simultaneous-load behavior or explain a historical RTX memory fault. Long thermal tests remain a later iteration, one GPU at a time as requested.

arcB70/thermal_watch.py provides passive paired telemetry; it never infers, switches models or changes cooling/power settings. Arc temperature, fan and power telemetry and live model context/slots are also exported to Prometheus/Grafana.

Evidence: sanitized bring-up receipt. See model guide, MCP guide, B70 preparation limits and earlier benchmark results.

Capacity-exhausted investigation

During live use, the owner ledger and native server both showed two genuinely processing primary requests, with no model-load error. This profile's maximum is two requests in parallel. Additional requests (including background work from an OpenCode conversation) receive HTTP 429 hardware_capacity_exhausted; the current gateway does not queue them. This is admission saturation, not a VRAM fault or stale slot count. A slot is an inference request, not a session.

Context cache is allocated for the fixed 256k/two-slot geometry even when the current prompts are shorter. A third 256k Q4 cache slot would require about 34.20 GiB including weights and the selected reserve, exceeding the board's 31.89 GiB usable memory. Active requests were not cancelled or restarted.
